overview: Chips: OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank are expanding Stargate with five new U.S. data center sites and a 4.5GW deal.
Big story: Anthropic's leaked IPO filing targets a $2 trillion valuation and flags AI's existential risk to humanity.

items.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Argon, its new frontier model
items.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 4 Argon, a frontier model built for complex coding, enterprise and cybersecurity workflows, rolling out first to trusted testers under its Fairwind Program. Google says it beats OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra on several benchmarks, intensifying competition among the top AI labs.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO filing targets $2 trillion valuation
items.summary: Anthropic's leaked IPO prospectus targets a roughly $2 trillion valuation, based on projected 2028 revenue of $190-200 billion, Reuters reported. The filing also lists AI's "existential risk to humanity" as a disclosed risk factor, an unusually candid admission for what could become the largest IPO on record.

items.headline: OpenAI unveils always-on 'Dots' agents at DevDay
items.summary: At its DevDay keynote, OpenAI unveiled Dots, always-on AI agents that run on dedicated cloud computers, plus plugin extensions letting developers build full apps inside ChatGPT. CEO Sam Altman also addressed safety concerns and said he has no set timeline for an IPO.

items.headline: Nvidia board approves $150 billion buyback increase
items.summary: Nvidia's board authorized an additional $150 billion in share repurchases, lifting total remaining authorization to $235 billion, the largest such increase in the company's history. Shares rose on the news, reflecting investor confidence in sustained AI-chip demand even as Nvidia commits heavily to data-center partnerships.

items.headline: OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank add five Stargate sites
items.summary: OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank are expanding the Stargate AI infrastructure program with five additional U.S. data center sites, building on the flagship Abilene, Texas campus already operating. The expansion underscores how much compute capacity leading labs believe they need for next-generation model training.

items.headline: OpenAI and Oracle advance Stargate with 4.5GW deal
items.summary: OpenAI and Oracle agreed to develop an additional 4.5 gigawatts of Stargate data center capacity in the U.S., extending their earlier infrastructure partnership. The deal adds to a buildout that already includes over 450,000 Nvidia GB200 GPUs planned for the Abilene, Texas site.

items.headline: Huawei's Ascend AI chips now outsell Nvidia in China
items.summary: Huawei has accelerated its next-generation Ascend 960DT chip launch to the first quarter of 2027, three quarters ahead of schedule, as its Ascend accelerators have overtaken Nvidia in Chinese sales and market share. The shift shows how U.S. export controls are pushing China's AI industry toward domestic chip suppliers.

items.headline: Microsoft merges Copilot into one enterprise AI assistant
items.summary: Microsoft is combining its consumer and workplace Copilot assistants into a single enterprise-focused product, ceding the crowded personal AI chatbot market to OpenAI, Google and Meta. Companies in Microsoft's Frontier program get early access to the merged Home, Code and Autopilot features in the coming weeks.

items.headline: Pichai posts CEO memo on Google's 'AI momentum'
items.summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai published a message to employees titled "The next chapter of our AI momentum," addressing the company's ongoing AI strategy. The post comes as Google pushes its newly launched Gemini 4 Argon model and faces intensifying competition from OpenAI and Anthropic.

items.headline: Moonshot's Kimi AI adopted by banks, VCs for research
items.summary: Chinese AI startup Moonshot said financial giants including investment bank CICC and venture firm Hong Shan, formerly Sequoia China, are using its Kimi models for research. Kimi users can pull data directly from S&P Global, Crunchbase and the U.S. SEC's EDGAR database, among other sources.

items.headline: Alibaba, ByteDance and Zhipu AI make Time's AI A-list
items.summary: Time magazine named Alibaba, ByteDance and Zhipu AI among its first AI A-list of influential companies, recognizing China's rapid progress in large language models. The listing signals growing international acknowledgment of Chinese AI labs even as U.S. export restrictions on advanced chips continue.

items.headline: Huang: AI distillation is 'competition,' not 'theft'
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC's Squawk Box that AI models learning from competitors' outputs through distillation is "competition," pushing back after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called the practice "theft." The exchange highlights friction over how Chinese AI firms train on Western models' outputs.

items.headline: Zuckerberg: AI superintelligence is 'now in sight'
items.summary: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said AI superintelligence is "now in sight," framing it as a tool for personal empowerment rather than concentrated corporate control. The comment came as Meta launched a new enterprise-focused AI business unit and leaned into "superintelligence" branding.

items.headline: Nadella: 'Trust is going to be the biggest issue'
items.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella told CNBC's Deirdre Bosa that trust will be the biggest challenge facing AI companies as autonomous AI systems gain more capability. His comments reflect growing industry focus on AI safety and user confidence as enterprise adoption accelerates.

items.headline: US raises pressure on China over chips before Xi-Trump talks
items.summary: The U.S. is tightening pressure on China over chip exports, oil sanctions and Iran ahead of planned talks between Trump and Xi Jinping, using export controls as a bargaining tool. The timing shows Washington linking AI chip policy to broader trade and geopolitical negotiations with Beijing.

items.headline: Trump: administration rebrands AI as 'super intelligence'
items.summary: Trump declared at the UN on September 22 that the U.S. government would replace "artificial intelligence" with "super intelligence" in official documents, a rebranding Meta's Zuckerberg has echoed. The shift reframes U.S. AI policy language around ambition rather than risk, as safety concerns mount industry-wide.

items.headline: China's State Council plans comprehensive AI legislation
items.summary: China's State Council issued a legislative work plan calling for comprehensive AI governance legislation, though regulators are taking an incremental approach with targeted rules rather than one sweeping law. The move reflects Beijing's effort to balance AI innovation with centralized oversight as the technology scales nationwide.

items.headline: EU's AI Act 'Digital Omnibus' delays high-risk deadlines
items.summary: The EU's Digital Omnibus on AI, in force since late July, postpones several high-risk AI system deadlines and simplifies parts of the AI Act's scope. A new ban on "nudifier" apps generating non-consensual intimate imagery takes effect in December, giving companies more time to comply.
